chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about the water of the bathhouse, and he said: “Enter it wearing a waist-wrapper, and do not perform ghusl from another water source unless there is a junub in it, or its people are many such that you do not know whether among them there is a junub or not.”
So this report is to be understood as referring to when the water has no source supply; for in that case, the contact of the junub with it renders it corrupted.

key_terms.بِإِزَارٍ: with a waist-wrapper, indicating proper covering
key_terms.تُفْسِدُهُ: renders it spoiled or unusable in the legal sense
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَاءِ الْحَمَّامِ: the water of the public bathhouse
key_terms.مَادَّةٌ: a supplying source that continuously feeds the water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using bathhouse water if a junub may have used it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of bathhouse water and proper etiquette when entering the bathhouse. It indicates caution regarding water used by a junub, and the closing statement explains that this applies when the water lacks a continuing source, in which case contact by a junub affects its purity.
